title: Normalized scalar pullback chain maps are naturally invertible on good representatives
statement: For a coefficient extension E→L of finite fields over Q_l and a scheme morphism f:X→Y, let I include the good integral E-complexes on Y and let k lift their termwise scalar extension to good L-complexes. Let t=I followed by the pullback chain functor over E and s the analogous inclusion and pullback chain functor over L. There is a unique natural isomorphism c:t⋙S_X⋙Q≅k⋙s⋙Q whose hom at every good P is Q(scalarPullbackChain(P)). The specified chain comparison is [lem-pur-integral-scalar-finite-comparison-models], and its quasi-isomorphism on good inputs is [lem-pur-integral-scalar-pullback-chain-quasi-iso].

source.place: Tensor reassociation, evaluation and coefficient comparisons; scalar-comparison proof step 9 of lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension; Stacks 03EL, 07A4, 08J9 and 08TC.

proof.text: Each prescribed localized chain map is invertible by the existing quasi-isomorphism theorem on good inputs. Chain naturality, followed by functoriality of Q, gives naturality of these components. Assemble their asIso values with NatIso.ofComponents. Its hom components are exactly the given Q-images. Equality of those hom components and extensionality of natural transformations and natural isomorphisms prove uniqueness. The private comparison used by the caller is chosen from this proved unique characterization, so its entire data is fixed by the displayed components.
